claim_summary: Within strictly positive one-step forward-Euler mass-action SIR with initially zero removed fraction, a transversal fall of the prevalence peak from day two to day one upon increasing transmission exists exactly for initial infectious fraction above 1/5; its peak-time cumulative attack jump is strictly below 2/5, with sharp unattained supremum.
integrity: Mathematical derivation and finite exact-rational tests are separate; verification is not external or independent. Numerical tests are not an exhaustive proof.
scientific_limitations: Applies only to one-step forward-Euler mass-action SIR, day-2-to-day-1 transversal switch, R0=0, gamma in (0,1), and local positivity of every state; no stochastic network or later-peak bounds. The source reports nonmonotonicity numerically, so only sharp extremal constants/characterization are proposed as new.
title: Sharp 20-percent seed threshold and 40-percent jump ceiling at the earliest SIR peak switch
